newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil tumbles again, buying still poor.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil tumbles again, buying still poor.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil prices fell hard again on Tuesday as poor demand in Europe mirrored weakness in markets to the East and West, traders said.

High sulphur barges traded in the morning at $99 and $98 a tonne fob ARA but then the offer fell sharply, reaching as low as $94, before a little buying from oil majors and traders brought numbers up by a dollar or two.

High sulphur cargoes met a similar fate, with numbers theoretically falling almost as far as barges. One utility player said he saw physical offers as low as $96 cif NWE by mid-afternoon. This follows trade on Monday at $101 cif U.K., for flexible dates in February.
Low sulphur fuel oil fell too, though not quite so far. Barges were quiet, but were assessed weaker by around $3 a tonne.
A cargo deal struck on Monday at the fob high of published quotes, for Scandinavian barrels, failed to influence prices as the buyer was expected to place the barrels into an existing commitment.
Offers into Italy were heard down as low as $115 cif Milazzo, but the main potential buyer was not heard to have been tempted by the lower numbers.
